_README: This file is managed by LazyCue (see shelley/lazycue). Do NOT edit by hand — it is the cached, machine-generated DSL for a self-healing browser test. To change behavior, edit the test description and re-run LazyCue.
description:
"The input" is the message input [data-testid="message-input"]; "the send button" is [data-testid="send-button"]; "the thinking indicator" is [data-testid="agent-thinking"]; "Queue it" means: the send options button [data-testid="send-options-button"] should be enabled and visible (up to 5s); click it; the queue option [data-testid="queue-option"] should become visible (up to 5s); click it. Call "saved text" returns the text the server keeps for the conversation's composer, or "(none)". Call "hold sends" makes the browser's message sends wait before they reach the server, call "sends held" counts those waiting, and call "release sends" lets them through. Perform the steps in order.
1. Navigate to /c/composer-requeue and wait (up to 30s) for the input to be visible.
2. Fill the input with "delay: 60"; the send button should become enabled (up to 5s); click it; the thinking indicator should become visible (up to 30s).
3. Fill the input with "continue".
4. Call "saved text"; it should become "continue" (up to 10s).
5. Call "hold sends"; it returns "holding".
6. Queue it.
7. The input's value should become exactly "" (up to 5s).
8. Call "sends held"; it should become "1" (up to 10s).
9. Fill the input with "continue".
10. Call "release sends"; it returns "released".
11. A queued badge [data-testid="queued-badge"] should become visible (up to 10s).
12. Call "saved text"; it should become "continue" (up to 10s).
13. The input's value is exactly "continue".
